newsitem.title: FRANCE: Ranarridh in France, to meet French official.
newsitem.headline: Ranarridh in France, to meet French official.

text.p: Cambodian First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh is still in France and is due to meet a French official later on Monday, a family member and official French sources said.

The family member told Reuters on Monday by telephone that an aide to French President Jacques Chirac would meet Prince Ranariddh later in the day in the southern town of Aix-en-Provence day where he is staying at the home of one of his sons.
But official French sources said that Ranariddh's meeting would be with a Foreign Ministry representative, rather than a presidential aide.
A Foreign Ministry spokesman declined all comment.

Ranariddh associates in France had said on Sunday that the prince had left France to return to Cambodia, where forces loyal to his rival, Second Prime Minister Hun Sen, appeared to be in complete control of Phnom Penh and its outskirts.
But on Monday, the same associates said that he had decided at the last moment on Sunday to delay his return.

"He delayed his return to denounce the coup d'etat, to seek the support of foreign governments and to hold a news conference in Paris on Tuesday," Sam Rainsy, a Ranariddh ally and former Cambodian finance minister told Reuters by telephone from Nimes, southern France, where he is on holiday.
France is the former colonial power in Cambodia, where about 2,000 French nationals still reside, according to the French Foreign Ministry.
The Asian nation was a French protectorate for 90 years until independence in 1953.
Fighting broke out in the streets of the capital Phnom Penh on Saturday after Hun Sen ordered a crackdown on "illegal troops" under Ranariddh's command.
Ranariddh, in statements issued in Paris on Saturday, accused Hun Sen of staging a coup d'etat in order to derail elections scheduled for May 1998.
But a radio station loyal to Hun Sen later denied the charge.
After two days of fighting, troops backing Ranariddh pulled out of Tang Krasang base near Phnom Penh's international airport, a Cambodian military intelligence official said.
Phnom Penh was calm but tense on Monday after the overnight curfew ended, although troops were seen looting the nearby airport, about 10 km (six miles) west of the capital.
All flights in and out of Phnom Penh have been cancelled since the weekend.
At least 12 people were killed and 50 wounded in the weekend's fighting on the streets of the capital.
